svg.text: One-file, crash-safe key-value database. Go standard library only.
= crash point named in the code
= can be lost if killed here (never ACKed)
A. WRITE PATH: from the client to the disk
ONE committer goroutine: one write at a time, so commit order is total
if killed right here, disk has:
W0 Admission: check the ops and compute the exact frame size F
= 56 + payload. Does it fit under max_bytes? If not: REWRITE
Tail repair (first write after open only): cut off a TORN tail
or restore a SHORT_SENTINEL, then fsync. Rule P4.
old tail fixed, valid data unchanged
W1 Stream the frame with pwrite at logical_end: 40 B header,
W2 The whole frame is in the file and fsync is running.
frame in the OS cache, not yet safe
W3 fsync returns: DURABILITY POINT. The frame is now on disk.
W4 Publish to the index under the WRITE lock: index,
logical_end and seq change together (rule P3).
W5 OnCommit hook: serve prints and flushes 'ACK id'. ACK order
Reply to the caller, then take the NEXT transaction. After the
reply, if 64 MiB were appended: checkpoint (KEYDIR frame,
Any write, fsync or rename error: the handle is POISONED, the caller gets ErrIO, and an fsync is never retried.
B. ON-DISK FILE LAYOUT (little-endian, sizes in bytes)
The index is NOT in the file. It lives in RAM and is rebuilt at open (from a KEYDIR frame or a scan).
Commit marker: there is no separate marker write. The 16-byte trailer IS the marker. A frame is valid only if its header
checks pass and its CRC64 covers every byte of header and payload, so a half-written frame can never look committed. One
BATCH payload: op_count u32, then per op: kind u8, key_len u16, value_len u32, key, value. One batch = one frame = all or
KEYDIR payload (checkpoint): checkpoint_seq u64, entry_count u64, then per key: key_len u16, key, value_off u64, value_len
Files: path (data), path.lock, path.create.tmp, path.compact.tmp. The temp files are never trusted and are deleted at open.
C. READS, THE IN-MEMORY INDEX, AND THE LOCKS
built at open, updated at step 6
MGET holds ONE RLock for all its keys, so a reader never sees half of a batch.
path.lock (flock): one process per database. A second opener gets ErrLocked. It locks a side file, not the data
file, so the data file can be replaced by rename.
Request channel + ONE committer goroutine: only one write runs at a time, so ACK order = commit order.
db.mu (RWMutex): readers hold RLock across lookup AND pread. The committer takes the write lock only briefly, to
submitMu (RWMutex): stops Close() racing with new writes. After Close, writes return ErrClosed.
stdout mutex (serve): each reply is one whole line, printed and flushed.
D. DISK-FULL GUARD (decided BEFORE any byte is written)
Work out S = size of the compacted
image after this write, and headroom
this write, swap it in (panel F)
A streamed batch (ApplyStream, over 64 MiB) can only APPEND, so near the cap it returns ErrFull instead of rewriting.
A delete-only write needs no headroom, so it can free space. The cap is saved in the superblock, so every later put or
E. RECOVERY when the database opens (writes ZERO bytes)
Take path.lock (ErrLocked if busy). Delete stale path.create.tmp and path.compact.tmp, so a half-
done creation or compaction is simply thrown away. File missing? Create it through a temp file,
Read superblock A and B. Valid = magic, version and sb_crc match. The valid slot with the highest
generation wins. A torn slot is ignored.
Is the checkpoint usable? ckpt_off and ckpt_seq must match a valid KEYDIR frame (same epoch, same
seq, its end = replay_start). Yes: load the index from it. No: scan from byte 8192.
Scan frames one by one: check magic, epoch, exact seq, header CRC, length, frame CRC64, end marker
and payload. Apply each good batch whole. STOP at the first bad frame.
Name the tail: COMPLETE (ends on a frame boundary), TORN (leftover bytes, ignored) or
SHORT_SENTINEL (frame is good but its last end-marker bytes are missing: kept). The index is now
If --max-bytes changed, write the inactive superblock and fsync. Start the committer and print
READY. Recovery wrote nothing to the data file. Tail repair waits for the first write.
F. COMPACTION / REWRITE (one replaceFile, writes pause)
Create path.compact.tmp (empty) with a NEW random epoch. The old file at path is untouched.
Stream the live keys, sorted, as packed frames (up to 4 MiB each), copying values from the
old file in chunks. A kill leaves a torn temp.
Append the KEYDIR frame, then write superblock slot A (checkpoint fields set, saved size cap
fsync the temp file. The replacement is complete and durable, but path is still the OLD file.
A kill here: the temp is never promoted.
rename(temp, path). Atomic: path names the old OR the new file, never a mix.
fsync the directory so the rename itself is durable BEFORE any ACK that depends on it.
Swap file handle + index + epoch + superblock + logical_end + seq under ONE write lock (rule
P3), then close the old file.
Kill before C5: the old file wins, the temp is deleted at the next open.
Kill after C5: the new file wins. Either way path always holds a complete, valid file.
Never publish an index entry that points at bytes until
those bytes are durable (fsync before step 6).
Never retire the old file until the replacement is complete
and durable (fsync before rename, close old last).
Never show a mixed state: file handle, index, epoch and
offsets swap under ONE write lock.
Never append behind a bad tail: repair TORN or
SHORT_SENTINEL and fsync before the first append.
Source of truth: docs/SPEC.md. The CP-xxx names are the crash points HYDRA's sweep mode kills at.
